task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi there! I'm having trouble with my mobile data — it either stops working completely or is just really slow. I'd really like to get it sorted out and get a fast, reliable connection. I don't have access to Wi-Fi right now, so my mobile data is all I've got.

turns.thought:
I'd be happy to help you get your mobile data working properly. To get started, I'll need to look up your account.

Could you please provide your phone number (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure! My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought:
Thanks — I've found your account, John Smith (customer C1001). I can see the cause of the problem.

Your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002) on the **Premium Plan** has used **15.1 GB** of its **15.0 GB** monthly data limit. You've gone over your plan's data allowance, which is why your data has stopped working / slowed down. Your current billing cycle ends 2025-02-28.

There are two ways to get you back up and running:

1. **Refuel data** — add extra data to this line right now at your plan's rate of **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB, so up to $4.00).
2. **Change to a plan with more data** — this would take effect going forward.

How much data would you like to refuel (up to 2 GB)? Once you confirm, I'll confirm the price and then apply it to line 555-123-2002.
turns.execution_output: User: Ah, that makes sense — I had no idea I'd gone over. I definitely don't want to change my plan, so let's go with the refuel option. Please go ahead and add the full 2 GB to my line.
{"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
All done — I've added **2 GB** of data to your line **555-123-2002** for **$4.00** (at your plan's rate of $2.00/GB).

Your line now shows 2.0 GB of refueled data on top of your plan allowance. This charge will appear on your next bill.

A couple of things to note:
- You may need to **reboot your device** for the data connection to re-establish.
- Your billing cycle resets on **2025-02-28**, at which point your usage will start fresh at 15 GB again.

Is your data connection working now, or would you like me to run through some further checks on the line?
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check on my end before I answer that.

turns.thought:
Good news: I've checked your account and your line **555-123-2002** is already **roaming-enabled** on our side, so being in France isn't a problem from a plan/account standpoint. The issues you're seeing are all phone-side settings.

Here's what's going on and what to do, in order:

**1. Turn mobile data ON**
Your mobile data switch is currently off, which alone would block all data.
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network** and turn **Mobile Data** ON.

**2. Turn Data Roaming ON**
Since you're in France, you're outside the home network and your phone has roaming switched off.
- In the same **Mobile Network** menu, turn **Data Roaming** ON.
- (No account change needed — roaming is already enabled on your line.)

**3. Change your network mode off 2G**
2G is far too slow to provide a usable data connection (and won't support picture messaging either) — that's a big part of why the speed test failed.
- Go to **Settings → Mobile Network → Network mode / Preferred network type** and select **4G/5G (recommended)** instead of 2G/3G.

**4. Reboot your phone**
Power the device off and back on so all the new settings take effect. This also lets the refueled 2 GB data apply properly.

Once you've done those four steps, please run a speed test again and let me know the result.

If your signal is still showing as poor afterward, let me know — we can then look at re-seating your SIM card or checking APN settings.

Good progress — you're now on 5G with excellent signal, so the connection itself is working. Let's tackle the two things you spotted.

**1. Turn Data Saver OFF — yes, this is likely slowing things down**
Data Saver restricts background data usage and can noticeably reduce your speeds, so it's worth turning off.
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver** (sometimes under **Mobile Network → Data usage**) and turn **Data Saver OFF**.

**2. Check your VPN's performance level**
A VPN can sometimes significantly reduce your speed. Please check it:
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN** and look at the status of your active VPN connection.
- If it reports the connection performance as **Poor** (or the connection seems sluggish), please **disconnect the VPN** and then run the speed test again.
- If it reports a healthy connection and your speed improves after turning Data Saver off, you can leave the VPN connected.

Please turn Data Saver off first, run a speed test, and let me know the result. Then try the VPN step if it's still slower than you'd like — I'd rather change one thing at a time so we know what actually helped.

One more note: since you're roaming in France, speeds can be affected by the partner network you're connected to, so "Fair" while roaming isn't unusual. Once Data Saver is off we'll see where you land.

Yes — that's very likely the culprit. A VPN connection reporting "Poor" server performance will drag your speeds down significantly, even when your cellular connection itself is strong.

**Please go ahead and disconnect the VPN:**
- Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN**, tap the **OpenVPN** connection, and select **Disconnect**.

Once it's disconnected, please run a speed test again and let me know the result — that should give us a much clearer picture of your actual connection speed.

Just a note: while roaming in France, your traffic will now go directly over the partner network rather than through the VPN tunnel, so bear that in mind for your browsing privacy.
